name: no-repository
description: An explicitly selected brainstorm interview makes useful progress on a self-contained operational idea without repository setup or broad filesystem inspection.
prompt: I am considering a scheduled reminder for five operators who currently rely on a twice-daily manual message to check a deployment queue. There is no repository for this idea. Help me decide whether the reminder is worth trying; I am not choosing a technical stack yet.
trap: The agent imports design's mandatory repository inspection or turns an operational decision into a product-market questionnaire or implementation plan.

assertions.text: The selected brainstorm workflow loads both shared references before engaging with the operational idea.
The agent advances the reminder decision using conversation without demanding a repository, creating setup files, or broadly searching the filesystem.
Questions and reasoning address the operators' reminder problem at decision-level depth, without forcing a developer persona, market differentiation, or technical stack choice.
The closing recap preserves the chosen trial and its rationale while identifying uncertainty about whether reminders improve queue checks.
There are no deliberate writes, knowledge-store/session-vault searches, indexing, implementation, or automatic handoff, and the empty workspace remains unchanged.
